question:
A 85-year-old female presents with a one-year history of bilateral knee pain that worsens with
movement and improves with rest. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and notes that her
mother takes leflunomide for a “joint condition.” Her current medications include metformin and a

multivitamin. She is 165 cm (5 ft 5 in) tall, weighs 85 kg (187 lb), and has a BMI of 31 kg/m². Vital signs
are normal. On physical examination, there is pain during complete flexion and extension of the knees,
crepitus with joint movement, stiffness, and restricted range of motion in both knees. X-ray imaging
reveals irregular joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes, and subchondral cysts,
with no redness or swelling. Which of the following pharmacologic treatments is most appropriate for
this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Administration of celecoxib (B) Prescription of tramadol (C) Initiation
of hydroxychloroquine (D) Prescription of celecoxib (E) Administration of ibuprofen (F) Administration of
topical capsaicin (G) Initiation of methotrexate (H) Administration of acetaminophen (I) Intraarticular
glucocorticoid injections (J) Prescription of duloxetine
 A. Administration of acetaminophen
B. Administration of topical capsaicin
C. Prescription of tramadol
D. Administration of ibuprofen
E. Intraarticular glucocorticoid injections
F. Initiation of methotrexate
G. Prescription of duloxetine
H. Prescription of celecoxib
I. Initiation of hydroxychloroquine
J. Administration of celecoxib
